bayts.text: To Him my words are addressed, on Saturday, in my homeland; and yesterday there appeared to me what has become a clear proof.
Yesterday You roused me: increase the outpouring (fayḍ) and the gnosis (maʿrifa), and forever, O Lord, illumine minds through me.
Make my return to my abode our happiness, and on the Day the creatures are gathered keep us from the fires (of Hell).
Grant me, by Your grace, to be forever a joy to the Muslims, and make our glad tidings everlasting in You.
Grant me possession today of something that never leaves me: glad tidings that in the two abodes stay close beside me.
I praise You with virgin praises, never spoken before, that I bring from the outpourings that pour down abundant as rains.
Lead to me endlessly openings (futūḥ) through which I may be glad tidings for whoever has embraced the guidance of Islam.
You are the All-Knowing (Al-ʿAlīm), who taught Your company that by which, through Your folding of distances (ṭayy), they outstripped one field after another.
Bring into being for me, today, an ease that makes it easy for me to recover, by Your bringing into being, what had been lost.
Make my heart firm, make my speech upright, and keep me from error of tongue, by annihilating what had been present (in the soul).
Make easy for me today, O Bestower (Al-Wahhāb), all that I hope for, and grant me precedence and pre-eminence.
You nurtured me, O Lord, in exile among enemies, until the time of my return to the homeland had come.
Grant Your humble servant possession of what he chooses from You, without scheming or deprivation, and make him docile and submissive.
Grant him possession, O Lord, out of generosity, of what surpasses every wish, O You who satisfy whoever has suffered hunger.
He has addressed You in intimate prayer, hoping You will not disappoint him: spare me, on the Day the creatures are raised, (the trial of) the Balance.
Frustrate forever the hope of whoever loathes him, since the year he was held back (in exile), when the Pilgrimage was his balance.
For him (Your servant) decree this year a reward without interruption, in all that he intends, for You, of adorning guidance.
Turn the hearts of all the enemies to his support, on land and on sea, O You who, if You will, make them yield.
He has addressed You in intimate prayer, hoping for what he longed for without delay, O Best of those to whom one turns, even the most impatient.
You are the Restorer (Al-Muʿīd), through whom I gain permanence in this world and the next: so grant me the return, O our Master.
I have left what was mine, by selling it, seeking what is with Him (Allah) who now fulfils my need.
O Opener (Al-Fattāḥ), Bestower (Al-Wahhāb), O Provider (Ar-Razzāq), O my King: open for me, give to me and provide for me by Your "Be!", with gentleness.
Remove my hardship without delay with gladness and aid, that I may raise pillars for the religion of God.
Make easy my return to Ṭūbā (Touba), protect me and keep me from the harm of creatures, and make my dwelling there pleasant for me.
Yours are the heaven, the earths and the air, without any partner: subdue for me whoever manifestly associates (others with You).
Answer, and pour forth blessing and peace upon the Support (As-Sanad), Muḥammad; and grant me an eminent and manifest gift.
